findings.title: The last MemberAffine survives the declared inter-recipe cleanup
findings.finding: The loop leaves factor bound to the final affine module. model.to(device) moves that module to CUDA. The cleanup deletes model and its named tensor collections, but never deletes factor. Python retains the local reference until one_recipe returns, so gc.collect and empty_cache cannot release this live module. Its tensors are released after empty_cache, leaving their allocator blocks cached before the next recipe. after_own_cleanup is recorded while the module remains live. This contradicts the claim that own tensor references are released and the current allocator cleared between cases. The source alone cannot establish the actual byte impact, but the reference lifetime is concrete.
findings.impact: The second recipe can inherit reserved allocator blocks, and after_own_cleanup is not a clean-case baseline. The recorded process peaks are still observations of the actual implementation; they should not be adopted as exact independently cold per-recipe measurements.
findings.requested_change: In a new sealed successor, confine private-factor initialization to a helper or delete its lingering module/tensor locals before cleanup; clear the allocator after all case CUDA references have ended, then take the cleanup snapshot before beginning the next recipe.

findings.title: Failures before stage/case registration can report a completed previous stage
findings.finding: Profile.stage sets active_stage but never clears it when the stage completes. one_recipe checks available memory before constructing/appending the case and before setting profile.case. Therefore a failed second-recipe memory precondition produces an overall failure receipt with only the first completed recipe in cases and an active_stage naming its completed final-custody stage. A failed first-recipe precondition similarly retains the completed data stage. The top-level failure stores type, message and traceback but no attempted recipe or explicit current preflight phase. Synchronization/reset/snapshot failures at stage entry also occur before stage registration.
findings.impact: Ordinary failure is caught and execution stops, but the machine-readable recipe/stage attribution can be missing or stale. Root custody should not have to infer which recipe failed from a completed prior stage or a traceback.
findings.requested_change: In a new sealed successor, register the attempted case/current phase before the recipe precondition, record stage-entry failures, and clear active_stage after successful completion. Keep an explicit active recipe/preflight field in the failure receipt.

findings.finding: numerical_imports obtains the actual runtime but checks equality before returning it. main assigns actual_runtime and torch_local only after that function returns.
